hints: Focus on what makes ethanal different from propanone, one is an aldehyde that is easily oxidised and the other is a ketone that resists mild oxidation.
Notice that ethanal is $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ and propanone is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, so both molecules contain the $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$ group.
Recall which test depends only on that $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$ group to give a yellow precipitate, as that test will give the same result for both compounds.
walkthrough:
**Identify the two compounds**

Think of them side by side like friends. Ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, is an aldehyde with a hydrogen attached to the carbonyl carbon. Propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, is a ketone with no such hydrogen.

That hydrogen makes aldehydes easy to oxidise to carboxylic acids, while ketones resist mild oxidising agents.

**Check the oxidation tests**

Acidified dichromate(VI), cold acidified manganate(VII) and Fehling's reagent are all mild oxidising agents. They oxidise aldehydes but not ketones.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + [O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$

**Check the iodoform test**

Alkaline aqueous iodine tests for the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group. Both compounds have it, and both give the yellow precipitate of triiodomethane, $\text{CHI}_3$.

$$\text{R-CO-CH}_3 + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 + \text{RCOO}^- + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Decide which cannot distinguish**

Since three reagents give a positive result with ethanal and a negative result with propanone, they can distinguish. The one that gives the same positive yellow precipitate with both cannot distinguish.

options.A: Acidified sodium dichromate(VI) can distinguish. It oxidises ethanal to ethanoic acid with a colour change from orange to green, while propanone shows no reaction under these conditions.
options.B: Alkaline aqueous iodine cannot distinguish. It is the iodoform test for the CH3CO group. Both ethanal and propanone contain this group, so both give a yellow precipitate of CHI3.
options.C: Cold acidified potassium manganate(VII) can distinguish. It oxidises ethanal and is decolourised from purple to colourless, while propanone does not react in the cold.
options.D: Fehling's reagent can distinguish. It oxidises ethanal to give a brick-red precipitate of copper(I) oxide, while propanone gives no reaction and stays blue.
